newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Oct 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Stockbroking firm Frankel Pollak has been cleared by the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) of any complicity with former director and convicted broker Greg Blank, but has admitted administrative errors relating to its activities between 1989 and 1991.

- The South African Revenue Service is losing at least 100 million rand a year through a growing tax-evasion scam in which diesel is spiked with paraffin and jet fuel -- oil products which attract little or no customs and tax.
- The Real Africa group has called a 300 million rand rights offer to increase its stake in managed health care company Lifecare and to fund future acquisitions.
- Frankel Pollak, the stockbroking firm, and three of its directors pleaded guilty on Thursday to breaking JSE rules and were fined 340,000 rand by the exchange.

- The publishing industry is attempting to force the government to decide whether or not it is going to nationalise the established school textbook publishing industry by allowing the various provincial governments to print textbooks in-house.
- Anglogold, Anglo's gold division, posted a three percent fall in profit in the quarter to September 30 as a rise in the rand gold price was more than offset by the rand's recent depreciation.

- The health department has instructed the state attorney's office to settle its legal dispute with SmithKline Beecham, the pharmaceutical group, just hours before the court deadline expired on Thursday.
- Executive directors at South African transport para-statal Transnet are paid close to one million rand a year, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau told parliament.

- Police are investigating two cases of culpable homicde against the builders of a Pretoria shopping complex after at least two people died and 18 were injured when a section of the building collapsed on Thursday.
